Title: FUN'S July 4 Cross Word Puzzle
Copyright: New York World
Date: 1914-06-28
Number: 25
Description: A 13-wide stepped diamond for the Fourth of July; an eagle with stars is printed over the shaded centre (r5c7, r6c6-c8, r7c5-c9, r8c6-c8, r9c7, shown as _), and the clues are all on Fourth of July themes.
Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-06-28, p. 84
Solution-Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-07-05, p. 81

intro: There is a fourth of July flavor to today's cross-word puzzle. You are invited to think of the Declaration of Independence and what it meant in 1776 and what it means today while you are trying to solve this puzzle. Fill in the small squares with words corresponding to the list of clews and definitions given below, allowing one letter of each word to each square. You will find the solution to this puzzle in next week's FUN. Meanwhile, see if you can solve it yourself.
solution heading: SOLUTION TO No 25 PUZZLE

_____WAR_____
____VALOR____
___PARADES___
__BIRD_EATS__

SORT_____IDEA

__SLIT_SUES__
___SCREAMS___
____EARNS____
_____PIE_____
______N______


## Clues
A2. It followed the Declaration of Independence. ~ WAR
A2 ^Printed: 2-3
A4. Displayed by Washington's soldiers. ~ VALOR
A4 ^Printed: 4-5
A6. Fourth of July celebrations are not complete without these. ~ PARADES
A6 ^Printed: 6-7
A8. The American eagle. ~ BIRD
A8 ^Printed: 8-9
A9. What everybody does at a fourth of July banquet. ~ EATS
A9 ^Printed: 10-11
A11. What orators will be on the fourth. ~ BUSY
A11 ^Printed: 12-13
A12. What tired marchers will feel ready to do after a long parade. ~ DROP
A12 ^Printed: 14-15
A14. One kind. ~ SORT
A14 ^Printed: 16-17
A15. An inspiration. ~ IDEA
A15 ^Printed: 18-19
A16. In a little while. ~ ANON
A16 ^Printed: 21-22
A18. To mark off distances from point to point. ~ SPAN
A18 ^Printed: 23-24
A19. To slash. ~ SLIT
A19 ^Printed: 25-26
A21. What a person does in instituting legal proceedings against another. ~ SUES
A21 ^Printed: 27-28
A22. What the American eagle does on the fourth of July. ~ SCREAMS
A22 ^Printed: 29-30
A24. Eagles. ~ EARNS
A24 ^Printed: 31-32
A24 ^Answer-Correction: ERNES
A24 ^Note: ERNES (sea eagles) is meant, but it doesn't fit the crossings; every letter of EARNS is clear in the key and checked by a down word
A25. Something good to eat. ~ PIE
A25 ^Printed: 33-34

D1. A festivity. ~ GALA
D1 ^Printed: 1-20
D2. To keep in safety. ~ WARD
D2 ^Printed: 2-9
D3. What Paul Revere did. ~ RODE
D3 ^Printed: 3-10
D4. To change. ~ VARY
D4 ^Printed: 4-13
D5. What the Declaration of Independence is on every fourth. ~ READ
D5 ^Printed: 5-14
D6. What we mustn't shoot off in New York City on July 4. ~ PISTOLS
D6 ^Printed: 6-29
D7. Displayed on every U. S. flag. ~ STRIPES
D7 ^Printed: 7-30
D8. What a firecracker does if you hold it too long. ~ BURNS
D8 ^Printed: 8-25
D10. Swallowed by millions on the fourth. ~ SODAS
D10 ^Printed: 11-28
D11. A neck wrap worn by women. ~ BOA
D11 ^Printed: 12-21
D13. Used in signing the Declaration of Independence. ~ PEN
D13 ^Printed: 15-24
D17. What we hope the weather will be on July 4. ~ NICE
D17 ^Printed: 22-31
D18. What the American school boys need not do on the fourth of July. ~ SUMS
D18 ^Printed: 23-32
D20. What Washington caught Cornwallis in. ~ TRAP
D20 ^Printed: 26-33
D21. The kind of celebration New York has every fourth. ~ SANE
D21 ^Printed: 27-34
D23. Beloved by every Irishman. ~ ERIN
D23 ^Printed: 35-36
